title: Fix Unix bounded-read cleanup: Darwin zombie-only group EPERM and confirmed post-reap absence
outcome: Apply the signal→reap→probe cleanup contract without treating EPERM as success or signaling a reused group; restore native macOS O1 probes while preserving Windows behavior.
acceptance: Preserve both original Mac runs and the standalone lifecycle discriminator, classify the Darwin zombie-only EPERM product defect, and cross-link the fix to the P-mac ruling 33ab140a723c479cadf43866c475dfd4.

Apply the Unix signal→reap→probe contract to bounded-read cleanup: signal the owned group while its leader is retained; reap; never send a non-zero signal to that numeric group after reap; a bounded post-reap kill(-G,0) probe confirms cleanup only on ESRCH, while persistent 0, EPERM or another uncertain result is Unresolved with both signal and probe errors. EPERM alone never grants success; Windows behavior is unchanged. An injectable syscall seam has fail-first tests for zombie-only EPERM followed by confirmed absence, live inaccessible members, surviving signalable descendants, persistent probes and the exact signal-before-reap/no-signal-after-reap sequence; exact-input focused checks pass.

The macOS lifecycle discriminator is covered by an integration test, the three original O1 failures pass after repair, and a standard-launcher Windows full gate plus standard-launcher focused macOS checks for the Darwin cleanup and original O1 failures pass on the exact reviewed input without weakening assertions or increasing existing timeouts.

An independent Codex+Claude read-only pair has no outstanding in-scope Medium-or-higher finding; exact source, review and gate evidence is recorded and handed to Merger/Opus2, with no push by this lane.
